claims.evidence: The witness sees used tires, but without sidewall markings or DOT codes, it is impossible to verify if they are high-quality imports (Tokunbo) or locally worn tires.

risks.risk: Tires may be expired or dangerously old.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the 4-digit DOT code on the sidewall of each tire.

risks.risk: Unknown size and specifications make them potentially incompatible with common vehicles.
risks.proof: A photo of the sidewall showing the size (e.g., 195/65R15).
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest, least valuable standard passenger car size.

risks.risk: Hidden structural damage such as sidewall bulges or internal patches.
risks.proof: A video showing the inner lining and both outer sidewalls of each tire.
risks.if_unproven: as having internal repairs or weak sidewalls.

risks.proof: A photo of a tread depth gauge or a coin inserted into the shallowest part of the tread.
risks.if_unproven: as tires at the legal wear limit.

proof_requests: Close-up photos of the sidewalls showing the brand, model, and size for every tire.
Photos of the 4-digit DOT manufacturing date codes.
Photos of the inner carcass of the tires to check for patches or plugs.
Clear shots of the tread depth for each tire.
response.reason: The witness report lacks all technical specifications including size, brand, and age, which are the primary drivers of tire value. No price can be determined without knowing what vehicles these fit.
